turns.content: Let X={1,...,n}, with n>1. Call a nonempty subcollection tight when its union is a proper subset of X and no element of X belongs to exactly one selected set. For 1<=k<=n-1 define P_k={1,...,k}, and for 2<=k<=n define Q_k={k,...,n}. Show that these 2n-2 distinct proper nonempty sets have no nonempty tight subcollection by choosing an element outside the union and finding an element covered exactly once.

For the upper bound, argue by induction on n. Assume a family B with no tight subcollection has at least 2n-1 members. Show that its members cannot have a common element by deleting such an element and applying induction on X with that element removed.
For each x in X, let B_x be the subfamily of members of B that do not contain X. Analyze these B_x, draw the resulting arrows, and deduce a directed cycle.

Choose a shortest directed cycle x1->x2->...->xk->x1. For each i, let Ai be the unique member of B that contains x_(i+1) but not x_i. Establish the properties of these witnesses, including that the Ai are distinct, that will be needed before any contraction.
Using the directed cycle and its uniquely witnessing sets, let X be the set of distinct witnessing sets and remove R from B. Determine how any remaining set can meet the cycle vertex set.

When k<n, replace the block X' by a new point x*. Define the image of every member of B' and prove that the image family consists of distinct, proper, nonempty sets and still has no tight subcollection.
When the cycle block X' is proper, let X be a new point replacing X'. Map a set containing the block to (S\X') union {x*}, and map a disjoint set to itself; then apply induction.
Handle separately the case k=n, then combine the upper bound with the prefix-suffix construction to state the largest possible cardinality.
